learning_outcomes.text: Explains the fundamental elements of classical and modern physics (mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics) and the stages of analyzing a characteristic physical phenomenon.
Compares classical theoretical models (e.g., Newton's laws) with modern ones (e.g., special relativity, introductory quantum mechanics).

Evaluates physical data in statistical terms (estimates of error types in physical measurements, evaluates the effects of systematic errors on experimental results, determines precision limits, interprets statistical tests for data validation).

Defines the general properties of forces in mechanical fields, uses calculations for automotive dynamic systems (e.g., Newton's second law, calculation of friction forces and moment of inertia in suspensions).
Defines the properties of mechanical waves and components of automotive systems (e.g., vibrations in springs, shock absorbers, mechanical resonance systems in chassis).
Uses calculations for energy/momentum conservation and interprets automotive dynamics experiments (e.g., momentum conservation in collisions, energy transfer in propulsion systems).
Defines terms such as force, kinetic energy, angular momentum, mechanical oscillations, expresses principles such as conservation of mechanical energy and thermodynamic laws applied in heat engines.
Performs precise physical measurements and analyzes characteristic phenomena using laboratory equipment (e.g., multimeters, sensors, voltage sources, oscilloscopes, signal generators).
Calculates, interprets, compares experimental results with theoretical predictions, identifying deviations and optimizing analysis methods.
Evaluates measurement errors in statistical terms (calculates random and systematic errors, determines uncertainties and detection limits in physical experiments).
Uses software (such as Excel, Origin, Matlab) for analysis and representation of physical data.
Graphically represents on millimeter paper the dependence between measured physical quantities, interprets and calculates parameters of interest (slope of a linear dependence).
Observes specific occupational safety norms in the physics laboratory.
Observes ethical principles, norms, and values.
Integrates into the working group and collaborates efficiently to solve work tasks.
Rigorously prepares study topics through continuous learning of newly introduced concepts.
Develops projects that integrate fundamental physics concepts into the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Fundamental notions. Scalar and vector physical quantities. Vector representation. Vector operations.
Elements of vector analysis. Derivation and integration of multivariable vectors. Differential vector operators.

Elements of classical mechanics. Kinematics of a material point (Trajectory and kinematic equations. Displacement vector, average velocity, instantaneous velocity. Average acceleration and instantaneous acceleration. Coordinate systems).

Elements of classical mechanics. Dynamics of a material point (Principles of Newtonian dynamics. Momentum. Torque. Angular momentum. Mechanical work and power. Kinetic energy. Potential energy. Conservative forces. Law of conservation of mechanical energy).
Elastic oscillations: Harmonic oscillatory motion; Damped oscillatory motion; Forced oscillatory motion; Composition of parallel and perpendicular oscillations.
Elastic waves: Definitions and classification. Propagation of a disturbance. Equation of a plane wave. Differential equation of waves. Propagation of waves in elastic media.
Phenomena specific to elastic waves: Huygens' Principle; Interference of elastic waves; Standing waves; Sound waves. Acoustic Doppler effect.
Notions of electrostatics: Electric charge. Coulomb's Law. Electric field. Electric field intensity. Electric potential. Electric flux. Gauss's Theorem. Local form of Gauss's Law.
Notions of electrokinetics: Direct electric current. Current density. Continuity equation (Law of conservation of electric charges). Electromotive force. Ohm's laws in integral and local form.

Notions of electrokinetics: Kirchhoff's Theorems. Resistor grouping, application of Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws in calculating equivalent resistance. Notions of magnetism: Magnetic field. Magnetic field induction; Magnetic field created by electric currents; Forces in the magnetic field (Lorentz force, Laplace force, Ampere force); Magnetic flux. Gauss's Law for magnetism.

Notions of electromagnetism: Law of the magnetic circuit. Electromagnetic induction. Faraday's Law. Self-induction. Electrodynamic field. Electromagnetic field. Maxwell's equations; Electromagnetic waves. Energy carried by electromagnetic waves. Electromagnetic spectrum.

Notions of electromagnetism: Phenomena specific to electromagnetic waves (Reflection. Refraction. Total reflection. Diffraction. Polarization). Elements of atomic physics: Atomic models. Atomic spectra. Energy levels. Elements of spectroscopy.
Elements of quantum mechanics: Photoelectric effect; Compton effect; Thermal radiation; Franck-Hertz experiment.

Elements of thermodynamics: Thermodynamic systems. Macroscopic and microscopic description of thermodynamic equilibrium states. Thermodynamic processes. Characteristic quantities. Kinetic theory of gases. Pressure formula. Distribution functions. Internal energy. Real gas. Equations of state. Principles of thermodynamics, applications.
Elements of solid-state physics: Generalities; Semiconductors; Semiconductor-based devices.
Specific and supplementary occupational safety instructions for the physics laboratory. Processing and acquisition of experimental data. Error calculation. Graphical representation.
L1. Study of forced oscillatory motion and resonance phenomenon.
L2. Determination of the speed of sound in air by composing perpendicular oscillations. Cathode ray oscilloscope.
L3. Determination of the specific charge of the electron by the magnetron method.
L4. Study of thermal radiation. Experimental verification of the Stefan-Boltzmann law.
L5. Ohm's Law. Determination of electrical resistance from the current-voltage characteristic.
Laboratory colloquium.
teaching_methods: Participatory lectures based on PowerPoint presentations and PDF course materials
5-10 minute recap of previous notions using open questions
Presentation of simple experiments in the classroom followed by theoretical explanations

assessment_methods.method: Final written exam (includes formative tests and case studies during the semester)
Laboratory activity and colloquium (completion of lab sheets and evaluation test)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Integer grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits. Passing conditions include understanding concepts of kinematics and dynamics, describing the motion of a material point, applying Newton's laws to determine dynamic quantities (momentum, moment, energy, mechanical work), and applying conservation principles (momentum, mechanical energy) in solving simple motion problems.
